title: #audramcdonald #gypsy #gypsymusical #gypsyrevival #gypsybroadway #gyp...
transcript: Okay, I've collected my thoughts on the Gypsy revival starring Audra McDonald. So, Mama Rose is one of the most iconic roles in American theatrical history, Gypsy is considered one of the greatest American musicals of all time, and Audra is the most Tony Award winning performer of all time — she's basically Broadway royalty. All of this makes Gypsy an easy sell but brings extremely lofty expectations. Overall, I thought this was a great production, but it definitely opens itself up to some subjectivity. Let’s start with Audra: her acting in the show is amazing and her singing is as beautiful as it has ever been, but it's quite a departure from the way the role is usually sung, as Audra's not a belter like Patti or Bernadette. I think this works for the way she portrays Rose, a bit more sweet and genuinely maternal than I've seen her played before, but I can't say I didn't miss the belting at the end of her two big solos. Something I’d suggest they do here is just bump up the volume of her and the orchestra, and in general I thought the volume of the whole show was kind of quiet for my taste. But back to Audra, she was great. She didn't floor me but I've seen her before and I know how amazing she is, so I feel like I had high expectations and she met them. I guess I'm just not sure this production made the case that Audra has to play this role specifically. Again, there's a double edged sword of her being so accomplished already, she can kind of do anything, but what makes Gypsy THE thing right now? Just some food for thought. Danny Burstein was wonderful as Herbie and Joy Woods was outstanding as Louise — her character arc was so well done. Honestly, everyone was great: the young kids, Jordan Tyson as June, the three strippers, Kevin Csolak as Tulsa. So many great moments from all these performers, but unfortunately everyone except Audra feels kind of underused just by virtue of how the show is structured. This might be a hot take, but the show is kind of disjointed in my opinion. So even though there's tons of stand out moments, they can't really come together in a way that leaves a singular impression. Again, that's just my opinion on the musical itself. But I digress. Unlike all Broadway productions before it, Rose and her daughters in this production are played by black actresses, which adds an interesting layer to the story’s themes of favoritism, the pressures to succeed, and personal agency. But other than the casting, I don't feel like this production drastically recontextualizes or stylistically changes the material. On the surface, it's still a very standard production of Gypsy. So at first I felt a little lackluster about it since it didn't like knock me over. But as I’ve sat with it, I'm definitely appreciating the direction by George C Wolfe which is a bit more understated and grounded than I think we've come to expect from this musical. In a lot of ways, this production feels like a play, and through that lens, I think I enjoy it more. The design elements were good, the sets are physical, they appear hand painted to me, and they're not very modern looking. But not in an outdated sort of way, more like an homage to old school Broadway sort of way. One area that did feel elevated by this production was the choreography. Gypsy is not considered a dance show, but what Camille A Brown has created here is notable and quite impressive. So yeah, a lot to unpack, I'm sure there will be a lot of discourse with this being such a well known show, but I personally enjoyed it and it's definitely worth seeing. If nothing else, you know it's an event when Audra’s involved. With that, another playbill for my collection.
reasoning: The reviewer clearly enjoyed the production and recommends it as 'definitely worth seeing,' praising multiple aspects including Audra McDonald's performance, the cast, and choreography. However, they express some reservations about missed opportunities and the production not fully justifying why this casting/interpretation was necessary.
